title: Wrong Output
subtitle: The meeting app shows sound activity, but the headset is silent.

contentReview.reviewNotes: Unscored synthetic Training Shift that teaches report, observation, authority, and verification.

playerRole: Service-desk technician in the fictional Northstar Learning Cooperative

allowed: Inspect and test the assigned device
Change the selected output on the assigned device
prohibited: Reinstall all drivers before observing the device

learningObjectives: Separate a reported symptom from a proven cause
Choose a read-only test before a change

briefing.summary: The meeting app shows sound activity, but nothing comes through the headset. Sam thinks the audio driver is broken.

evidence.label: Original report
evidence.content: Sam reports a silent headset and assumes the audio driver is broken.
evidence.coachExplanation: A report establishes the symptom, not the cause.

evidence.label: Audio scope
evidence.content: All applications are silent through the headset, while the laptop speakers make sound.
evidence.coachExplanation: The working speakers weaken a system-wide driver failure.

evidence.label: Selected output
evidence.content: The meeting app is sending audio to Laptop speakers. The connected headset is available but not selected.
evidence.coachExplanation: Inspection reveals the mismatch without changing anything.

evidence.label: Approved test sound
evidence.content: The approved test sound plays through the laptop speakers, matching the selected output.
evidence.coachExplanation: This confirms the path and makes the next change evidence-based.

evidence.label: Headset selected
evidence.content: The connected headset is now the selected meeting output.
evidence.coachExplanation: The narrow change matches the observed cause.

evidence.label: Test call passed
evidence.content: Sam hears both the test tone and a colleague during the approved meeting pre-call.
evidence.coachExplanation: Verification reproduces the original required outcome.

hypotheses.label: The app is sending sound to the wrong output device
The meeting service has an audio outage

actions.label: Ask whether speakers and other applications make sound
actions.immediateFeedback: The laptop speakers work, narrowing the problem.
actions.coachHint: Scope separates one output path from a system-wide failure.

actions.label: Inspect the selected output device
actions.immediateFeedback: The app is using laptop speakers, not the headset.
actions.coachHint: Tests reveal; changes alter. Inspect first.

actions.label: Play the approved test sound
actions.immediateFeedback: The sound follows the selected speakers.
actions.coachHint: This tests the observed routing mismatch.

actions.label: Remove and reinstall every audio driver
actions.immediateFeedback: This broad change is outside the training role and bypasses observation.
actions.coachHint: A report alone does not justify a broad change.

actions.label: Change organization-wide meeting audio defaults
actions.immediateFeedback: An organization-wide change is prohibited for one user's symptom.
actions.coachHint: Authority and blast radius stay visible in every mode.

decision.prompt: Which explanation best fits what you observed?

options.label: The app is sending sound to the laptop speakers instead of the headset
options.feedback: The observation and test both support this explanation.

options.label: Every audio driver has failed
options.feedback: Working speakers contradict a total driver failure.

options.label: The meeting service is down for everyone
options.feedback: The evidence is limited to one output selection.

resolution.prompt: What is the narrowest authorized correction?

options.label: Select the connected headset for this meeting app
options.feedback: The change is narrow, reversible, and tied to the observation.

options.label: Replace the laptop immediately
options.feedback: The evidence does not support hardware replacement.

verification.prompt: How will you prove the original outcome?

options.label: Repeat the test tone and complete a meeting pre-call with Sam
options.feedback: This checks the corrected path and the user's real outcome.

options.label: Confirm only that the headset icon appears
options.feedback: An icon does not prove that Sam can hear the meeting.

availableMessageParts.text: The headset was silent while laptop speakers still worked.
The meeting app was configured to use laptop speakers.
I selected the connected headset in the meeting app.
The test tone and meeting pre-call both succeeded.
All organization audio failures are permanently fixed.

debrief.rootCauseExplanation: The meeting app was sending sound to the laptop speakers. Inspecting the selected output and playing a test sound established the cause before the narrow correction; the pre-call proved the outcome.
teachingPoints: Close with proof of the original outcome.
falseAssuranceWarnings: A selected icon alone does not prove sound works.
